records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה בֶן־אֲמַצְיָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: In year twenty and seven year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah.
pieces: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.

L.1: In [the] twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah reigned.

R.1: Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah. It was the twenty-seventh year that Jeroboam had been king of Israel.

decisions.choice: Azariah: the king also called Uzziah
decisions.reason: Kings calls this king Azariah in verses 1-8, 17, 23 and 27, and Uzziah in verses 13, 30, 32 and 34. Chronicles and the prophets call him Uzziah (2 Chronicles 26; Isaiah 1:1; 6:1). The names are close in meaning: Azariah is "Yahweh has helped" and Uzziah "Yahweh is my strength". He is one king with two names, and each verse keeps the name it uses.

decisions.choice: the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam: a date hard to fit with 14:23
alternatives: the fifteenth year (by the figures of chapter 14)
decisions.reason: By 14:2 and 14:23, Jeroboam began in Amaziah's fifteenth year and Amaziah reigned twenty-nine years, so Azariah would have become king in Jeroboam's fifteenth year. The number here may count from a time when Jeroboam shared the throne with his father, or Azariah's reign may be counted from a different starting point. The Hebrew gives no explanation.

decisions.choice: reigned: became king
decisions.reason: With a date, the verb marks the start of the reign, as in each accession formula of Kings.

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date second
decisions.reason: Readable splits the accession formula into two sentences, as these books allow.

records.heading: Azariah king of Judah

records.source: בֶּן־שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְכָלְיָ֖הוּ מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: A son of six-teen year[s] he was when he became king, and fifty and two year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
pieces: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

L.2: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

R.2: He was sixteen years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a son of sixteen years: sixteen years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: fifty-two years: a reign that may include years shared with others
decisions.reason: This is one of the longest reigns in Kings. For part of it his son Jotham ruled for him (verse 5), and the count may also include years when he ruled beside his father Amaziah (14:21-22).

decisions.choice: the name of his mother: the queen mother
decisions.reason: For each king of Judah, Kings names his mother, who held an honored place at court (1 Kings 2:19; 15:13).

decisions.choice: sixteen years old
decisions.reason: Every level gives the age in the normal English way (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done Amaziah his father.
pieces: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his father Amaziah had done.

L.3: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

R.3: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, just as his father Amaziah had done.

decisions.choice: did the right in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict on a good king
decisions.reason: This is the verdict formula of Kings for a king who served Yahweh. Like his father's (14:3-4), the praise is limited by what follows: the high places stayed (verse 4).

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The verdict formula has one wording at each level throughout these books.

records.source: רַ֥ק הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא־סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Only the high places not were removed; still the people [were] sacrificing and making smoke at the high places.
pieces: However, the high places were not removed; the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

L.4: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.

R.4: But the hilltop shrines were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the hilltop shrines.

decisions.choice: the high places: local places of worship
decisions.reason: High places were local shrines, often on hills, with an altar. Even when Yahweh was worshiped there, sacrifice at them went against the law's demand to worship at the one place Yahweh chose (Deuteronomy 12:13-14). The same was said of Amaziah (14:4) and will be said of Jotham (verse 35).

decisions.choice: making smoke: burning incense, or burning offerings
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke. It can refer to incense or to parts of an offering. With "sacrificing" it describes the regular worship at the shrines.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "high places"; Readable says "hilltop shrines", as these books do throughout.

records.source: וַיְנַגַּ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיְהִ֤י מְצֹרָע֙ עַד־י֣וֹם מֹת֔וֹ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּבֵ֣ית הַחָפְשִׁ֑ית וְיוֹתָ֤ם בֶּן־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־הַבַּ֔יִת שֹׁפֵ֖ט אֶת־עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And struck Yahweh the king, and he was [one] with scale disease until [the] day of his death, and he dwelt in [the] house of the freedom; and Jotham son of the king [was] over the house, judging [the] people of the land.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} struck the king, and he had a serious skin disease until the day he died. He lived in a separate house, while Jotham the king's son was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck the king, and he was [one] with scale disease until the day of his death, and he lived in the separate house; and Jotham the son of the king [was] over the house, judging the people of the land.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} struck the king with a serious skin disease, and he had it until the day he died. He lived in a house by himself. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and ruled the people of the land.

decisions.choice: struck with scale disease: a skin disease that made him unclean, not modern leprosy
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in Leviticus 13-14 for a group of skin conditions that made a person unclean. It is not the same as leprosy as known today. Such a person had to live apart from others (Leviticus 13:46), as Miriam did (Numbers 12:10-15). Kings says only that Yahweh struck him; 2 Chronicles 26:16-21 says it happened when he went into the temple to burn incense, a task kept for the priests.

decisions.choice: the house of freedom: a separate house, where he lived apart
alternatives: a house of freedom, where he was released from duty
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for "free" (Exodus 21:2), so the phrase is literally "the house of freedom" or "of release". It may mean a house where the king lived released from his duties, or simply a house set apart because of his disease. The same phrase is used in 2 Chronicles 26:21. Its exact sense is not known.

decisions.choice: over the house: in charge of the royal household
decisions.reason: "Over the house" is the title of the steward who ran the palace (1 Kings 4:6; 16:9; 18:3). Here the king's son takes that place and acts for his father.

decisions.choice: judging the people of the land: governing the people of Judah
decisions.reason: To judge here is to govern, as the leaders in Judges did, not only to hear court cases. "The people of the land" are the people of Judah at large (11:14, 18-20). Jotham ruled for his father until he became king himself (verse 32).

decisions.choice: scale disease (Literal); serious skin disease (Balanced, Readable); separate house / a house by himself
decisions.reason: The wording for the disease follows Leviticus 13. Readable joins "struck" and the disease into one clause, and says "a house by himself" for the separate house.

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י עֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Azariah and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.

L.6: And the rest of the matters of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

R.6: Everything else Azariah did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: the royal record of Judah, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Judah, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Azariah. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: The question form means "they are written there".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As with every use of this formula in Kings, the question stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable: "the Book of the History of the Kings of ..." (Balanced), "the history of the kings of ..." (Readable).

decisions.choice: the rest of the matters of Azariah: more is told in 2 Chronicles 26
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells of his wars, buildings and army, and how his disease came on him (2 Chronicles 26:1-23).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב עֲזַרְיָה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹתָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Azariah with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in [the] city of David, and reigned Jotham his son in his place.
pieces: Then Azariah rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His son Jotham became king in his place.

L.7: And Azariah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David, and Jotham his son reigned in his place.

R.7: Then Azariah died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jotham became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died and joined his ancestors
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of death as lying down to rest with those who died before. It is used of kings who died a natural death.

decisions.choice: buried with his fathers in the City of David
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 26:23 adds that because of his disease he was buried in a field near the royal tombs, not in them.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula has one wording at each level in these books. Balanced and Readable say "was buried" for "they buried him".

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ זְכַרְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יָרָבְעָ֧ם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן שִׁשָּׁ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: In year thirty and eight year of Azariah king of Judah reigned Zechariah son of Jeroboam over Israel in Samaria six months.
pieces: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned six months.

L.8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.

R.8: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year that Azariah was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for only six months.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Jeroboam: the last king of Jehu's family
decisions.reason: His father was Jeroboam the second, whose long reign is told in 14:23-29. Zechariah was the fourth descendant of Jehu to rule, and with his death Jehu's line ends (verse 12).

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Omri built Samaria as his capital (1 Kings 16:24), and the kings of Israel ruled from it until its fall (17:6).

decisions.choice: only six months
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to bring out how short the reign was, which the Hebrew shows by giving it in months.

records.heading: Zechariah king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָ֑יו לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מֵֽחַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh as had done his fathers; not he turned aside from [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he caused to sin Israel.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.

L.9: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his fathers had done; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

R.9: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat: the calf worship at Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: This is the first Jeroboam, the founder of the northern kingdom, not Zechariah's father Jeroboam (14:23). He set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and his own priests and feasts (1 Kings 12:28-33), and Kings judges every king of Israel by whether he turned from that worship. "His fathers" here are the kings of Jehu's line before him, all judged the same way (10:31; 13:2, 11; 14:24).

decisions.choice: made Israel sin: caused the people to sin
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative form of "sin". Jeroboam's guilt is not only his own sin but leading the whole nation into it.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin (Literal); led Israel to sin (Balanced); led Israel into sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 3:3: one wording at each level for this formula, which closes the verdict on almost every king of Israel. "Turn aside from" is "turn away from" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula has one wording at each level throughout these books.

records.source: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן־יָבֵ֔שׁ וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ קָֽבָלְ־עָ֖ם וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And conspired against him Shallum son of Jabesh, and struck him before [the] people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
pieces: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against him. He struck him down in front of the people, killed him and became king in his place.

L.10: And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him before [the] people and killed him, and reigned in his place.

R.10: Shallum son of Jabesh made plans against Zechariah. He attacked him in front of the people and killed him. Then Shallum became king in his place.

decisions.choice: before the people: in public
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "before people", using a rare word for "before" that is found mostly in Aramaic. Some Greek manuscripts read "in Ibleam" instead, a town near where Jehu's men struck down King Ahaziah (9:27); the two readings differ by only a few letters. If that reading is right, Jehu's line ended near the place where his bloodshed began. The Hebrew is kept here.

decisions.choice: conspired: plotted to overthrow the king
decisions.reason: The verb means to bind together, and so to form a plot. It is the word used for each overthrow of a king in this chapter (verses 15, 25, 30).

decisions.choice: Zechariah ... Shallum
decisions.reason: Readable names the two men where the Hebrew says "him" and "he", since there are two kings in the sentence.

records.source: וְיֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֑ה הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Zechariah, look, they [are] written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Zechariah are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.11: And the rest of the matters of Zechariah, look, they [are] written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

R.11: Everything else Zechariah did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record of Israel, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Israel, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Zechariah. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: look, they are written (Literal); a plain statement (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says "look, they are written" instead of asking "Are they not written?" (verse 6). Balanced and Readable state both forms the same way, with the source named as everywhere in Kings.

records.source: ה֣וּא דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר אֶל־יֵהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּנֵ֣י רְבִיעִ֔ים יֵשְׁב֥וּ לְךָ֖ עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃פ
records.gloss: It [was the] word of Yahweh which he spoke to Jehu, saying, Sons of fourth [generation] will sit for you on [the] throne of Israel; and it was so.
pieces: This was the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to Jehu: "Your sons will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation." And so it happened.

L.12: That [was] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to Jehu, saying, "Sons of the fourth [generation] shall sit for you on the throne of Israel." And it was so.

R.12: This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised Jehu: "Your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel down to the fourth generation." And that is what happened.

decisions.choice: the word to Jehu: the promise of 10:30, now fulfilled
decisions.reason: Yahweh had told Jehu that, because he had destroyed Ahab's house, his sons to the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne (10:30). Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam and Zechariah were those four; with Zechariah's death after six months the promise reaches its end.

decisions.choice: and it was so: Yahweh's word came true
decisions.reason: Kings often notes that events happened as Yahweh had spoken (1 Kings 15:29; 16:12; 2 Kings 10:17). Here it marks both the gift of four generations and its limit.

decisions.choice: sons of the fourth generation for you: your descendants down to the fourth generation
decisions.reason: "Sons" here are descendants, and "for you" means they belong to Jehu's line.

decisions.choice: your sons (Balanced); your descendants (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "for you" into "your". Readable says "descendants" because they are great-grandsons and more, not sons, and "promised" for "the word ... spoke", since this was a promise.

records.source: שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן־יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְעֻזִיָּ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ יֶֽרַח־יָמִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Shallum son of Jabesh reigned in year thirty and nine year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a month of days in Samaria.
pieces: Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned one full month in Samaria.

L.13: Shallum son of Jabesh reigned in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a month of days in Samaria.

R.13: Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year that Uzziah, also called Azariah, was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for only one month.

decisions.choice: Uzziah: the same king as Azariah in verses 1-8
decisions.reason: Here Kings uses his other name, Uzziah, as it does again in verses 30, 32 and 34; verses 17, 23 and 27 go back to Azariah. Both names refer to the one king of Judah (see the note on verse 1).

decisions.choice: a month of days: a full month
decisions.reason: "A month of days" means a whole month (Genesis 29:14). Shallum's reign was the shortest so far in this chapter.

decisions.choice: Uzziah, also called Azariah
decisions.reason: Readable adds the other name so a reader does not think a new king of Judah has appeared. Literal and Balanced keep the name the verse uses.

decisions.choice: one full month (Balanced); only one month (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both say plainly what the idiom means.

records.heading: Shallum king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּעַל֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן־גָּדִ֜י מִתִּרְצָ֗ה וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיַּ֛ךְ אֶת־שַׁלּ֥וּם בֶּן־יָבֵ֖ישׁ בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיְמִיתֵ֖הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And went up Menahem son of Gadi from Tirzah, and he came [to] Samaria, and he struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and reigned in his place.
pieces: Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria. He struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, killed him and became king in his place.

L.14: And Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came [to] Samaria, and he struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and reigned in his place.

R.14: Then Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah to Samaria. He attacked Shallum son of Jabesh there and killed him. Then Menahem became king in his place.

decisions.choice: Tirzah: an older royal city of Israel
decisions.reason: Tirzah had been the capital of the northern kingdom before Omri built Samaria (1 Kings 14:17; 15:33; 16:23-24). It lay a short distance northeast of Samaria.

decisions.choice: went up ... came: marched on Samaria
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe a move against the capital. The text does not say who Menahem was before this; verse 16 shows him with soldiers at his command.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שַׁלּ֔וּם וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר הִנָּ֣ם כְּתֻבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Shallum and his conspiracy which he conspired, look, they [are] written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he carried out, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.15: And the rest of the matters of Shallum, and his conspiracy that he conspired, look, they [are] written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

R.15: Everything else about Shallum, and how he plotted to take the throne, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record of Israel, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Israel, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Shallum. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: look, they are written (Literal); a plain statement (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says "look, they are written" instead of asking "Are they not written?" (verse 6). Balanced and Readable state both forms the same way, with the source named as everywhere in Kings.

decisions.choice: his conspiracy that he conspired: the plot he carried out
decisions.reason: Noun and verb from the same root stress the deed, as with Zimri's plot (1 Kings 16:20). The source is said to tell more of it.

records.source: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה־מְ֠נַחֵם אֶת־תִּפְסַ֨ח וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤הּ וְאֶת־גְּבוּלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִתִּרְצָ֔ה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א פָתַ֖ח וַיַּ֑ךְ אֵ֛ת כָּל־הֶהָ֥רוֹתֶ֖יהָ בִּקֵּֽעַ׃פ
records.gloss: Then struck Menahem Tiphsah and all who [were] in it and its territories from Tirzah, because not it opened, and he struck [it]; all its pregnant women he ripped open.
pieces: At that time Menahem attacked Tiphsah and everyone in it and its territory, starting from Tirzah, because they would not open the gates to him. He struck it down, and he ripped open all its pregnant women.

L.16: Then Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who [were] in it and its territory, from Tirzah, because it did not open [to him]; and he struck [it]; all its pregnant women he ripped open.

R.16: At that time Menahem set out from Tirzah and attacked the town of Tiphsah, its people and the land around it. He did this because they would not open the town gates to let him in. He destroyed the town, and he even cut open all the pregnant women there.

decisions.choice: Tiphsah: the town Menahem attacked
decisions.reason: The only other Tiphsah in the Bible is on the Euphrates, at the far northern edge of Solomon's rule (1 Kings 5:4), which seems too distant for a raid starting from Tirzah. Some Greek manuscripts read Tappuah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim near the border with Manasseh (Joshua 16:8; 17:7-8). Either Menahem's power reached further than this short account says, or the name was changed in copying. The Hebrew is kept here.

decisions.choice: from Tirzah: starting out from Tirzah
alternatives: its territory as far as Tirzah
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that Menahem set out from Tirzah, as in verse 14, or that the territory he struck stretched as far as Tirzah. Both describe the same campaign.

decisions.choice: it did not open: the town would not open its gates to him
decisions.reason: To open to an attacker is to surrender (Deuteronomy 20:11). Menahem punished the town for holding out against him.

decisions.choice: ripped open the pregnant women: a cruelty of war
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the prophets name this as the act of foreign enemies (8:12; Hosea 14:1; Amos 1:13). Here an Israelite king does it to an Israelite town; the text states it without comment.

decisions.choice: open the gates to him (Balanced); open the town gates to let him in (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "did not open" refers to (m3). Readable puts "from Tirzah" first as the starting point and adds "the town of" and "even" to make the sentence clear.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן־גָּדִ֧י עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: In year thirty and nine year of Azariah king of Judah reigned Menahem son of Gadi over Israel ten years in Samaria.
pieces: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.

L.17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi reigned over Israel ten years in Samaria.

R.17: Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year that Azariah was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for ten years.

decisions.choice: the thirty-ninth year: the same year Shallum came to the throne
decisions.reason: Shallum began to reign in this year and was killed a month later (verse 13), so Menahem took the throne in the same year. The verse goes back to the name Azariah (verse 13).

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date in the first
decisions.reason: Readable splits the accession formula into two sentences, as in verse 8.

records.heading: Menahem king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֠ר מֵעַ֨ל חַטֹּ֜אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־יָמָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh; not he turned aside from [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he caused to sin Israel all his days.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. All his life he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.

L.18: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, all his days.

R.18: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. As long as he lived, he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: the calf worship Jeroboam set up at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-33).

decisions.choice: all his days: the end of this verse
alternatives: In his days Pul king of Assyria came (joined to verse 19)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "all his days" at the end of the verdict, which is unusual for this formula. The Greek versions read "in his days" and join it to the next verse: "In his days Pul king of Assyria came". The Hebrew division is kept; the sense of both is close.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: As in verse 9. Balanced and Readable move "all his days" forward so it is clear that it goes with "did not turn away".

records.source: בָּ֣א פ֤וּל מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֤ן מְנַחֵם֙ לְפ֔וּל אֶ֖לֶף כִּכַּר־כָּ֑סֶף לִהְי֤וֹת יָדָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ לְהַחֲזִ֥יק הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Came Pul king of Assyria against the land, and gave Menahem to Pul a thousand talent[s] of silver, to be his hands with him, to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.
pieces: Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul {{units:about 37 tons|1,000 talents}} of silver so that he would support him and strengthen his hold on the kingdom.

L.19: Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, so that his hands would be with him, to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.

R.19: Pul king of Assyria invaded the land. Menahem gave Pul {{units:about 37 tons|1,000 talents}} of silver to get his help, so that Menahem could keep a firm hold on his kingdom.

decisions.choice: Pul king of Assyria: Tiglath-pileser
decisions.reason: Pul is another name for Tiglath-pileser the third, the king of Assyria named in verse 29. 1 Chronicles 5:26 names him both ways. Pul was the name he went by as king of Babylon. Assyria, centered on the upper Tigris, was then the great power of the region.

decisions.choice: for his hands to be with him: to give him his support
decisions.reason: Having someone's hands with you means having their help and backing (1 Samuel 22:17).

decisions.choice: to strengthen the kingdom in his hand: to secure his rule
decisions.reason: Menahem had taken the throne by force (verse 14). The payment bought Assyria's backing, so that his hold on the throne would be firm.

decisions.choice: about 37 tons (1,000 talents)
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds, so a thousand talents was about 75,000 pounds. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the talent as the alternative.

records.source: וַיֹּצֵא֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם אֶת־הַכֶּ֜סֶף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַחַ֔יִל לָתֵת֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר חֲמִשִּׁ֧ים שְׁקָלִ֛ים כֶּ֖סֶף לְאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְלֹא־עָ֥מַד שָׁ֖ם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And brought out Menahem the silver on Israel, on all [the] mighty [men] of wealth, to give to [the] king of Assyria, fifty shekels silver for each man; and turned back [the] king of Assyria, and not he stayed there in the land.
pieces: Menahem raised the silver from Israel, from all the wealthy men, to give to the king of Assyria: {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|fifty shekels}} of silver from each man. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.

L.20: And Menahem brought out the silver from Israel, from all the mighty [men] of wealth, to give to the king of Assyria, fifty shekels of silver for each man; and the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.

R.20: Menahem got the silver by making every rich man in Israel pay {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|fifty shekels}} of silver, so that he could give it to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria went back home and did not stay in the land.

decisions.choice: brought out the silver on Israel: raised it as a levy
decisions.reason: The verb "bring out" with "on" means to impose a charge on someone and collect it. Menahem did not pay from the treasuries, as kings of Judah did (1 Kings 15:18), but taxed his people.

decisions.choice: mighty men of wealth: men of property
decisions.reason: The phrase often means warriors, but here, as of Boaz (Ruth 2:1), it means men of means, the landowners who could pay.

decisions.choice: fifty shekels each: a levy on about sixty thousand men
decisions.reason: A talent was 3,000 shekels (Exodus 38:25-26), so 1,000 talents was 3,000,000 shekels. At fifty shekels a man, about 60,000 men paid.

decisions.choice: about 1 1/4 pounds (fifty shekels)
decisions.reason: A shekel was about 2/5 ounce, so fifty shekels was about 20 ounces. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit. Readable says "went back home" for "turned back".

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י מְנַחֵ֖ם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Menahem and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.21: And the rest of the matters of Menahem and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.21: Everything else Menahem did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record of Israel, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Israel, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Menahem. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: The question form means "they are written there".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As with every use of this formula in Kings, the question stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable: "the Book of the History of the Kings of ..." (Balanced), "the history of the kings of ..." (Readable).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב מְנַחֵ֖ם עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ פְּקַחְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Menahem with his fathers, and reigned Pekahiah his son in his place.
pieces: Then Menahem rested with his ancestors, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.

L.22: And Menahem lay down with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.

R.22: Then Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died a natural death
decisions.reason: Of the kings of Israel in this chapter, Menahem alone dies this way and passes the throne to his son; the others are killed by plotters (verses 10, 14, 25, 30).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in verse 7.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַת֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ פְּקַֽחְיָ֨ה בֶן־מְנַחֵ֧ם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: In year fifty year of Azariah king of Judah reigned Pekahiah son of Menahem over Israel in Samaria two years.
pieces: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.

L.23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned over Israel in Samaria two years.

R.23: Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel in the fiftieth year that Azariah was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for two years.

decisions.choice: reigned: became king
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, with a date the verb marks the start of the reign.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable splits the accession formula, as in verse 8.

records.heading: Pekahiah king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מֵֽחַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh; not he turned aside from [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he caused to sin Israel.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.

L.24: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

R.24: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: the calf worship at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-33).

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded as in verse 9.

records.source: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֣ר עָלָיו֩ פֶּ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֜הוּ שָׁלִישׁ֗וֹ וַיַּכֵּ֨הוּ בְשֹׁמְר֜וֹן בְּאַרְמ֤וֹן בֵּית־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־אַרְגֹּ֣ב וְאֶת־הָאַרְיֵ֔ה וְעִמּ֛וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י גִלְעָדִ֑ים וַיְמִיתֵ֖הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And conspired against him Pekah son of Remaliah his officer, and struck him in Samaria in [the] citadel of [the] house of the king, with Argob and with the Arieh, and with him fifty men of [the] sons of [the] Gileadites; and he killed him and reigned in his place.
pieces: Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, plotted against him. He struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the royal palace, along with Argob and Arieh. Fifty men of Gilead were with Pekah. He killed Pekahiah and became king in his place.

L.25: And Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him, and struck him in Samaria, in the citadel of the house of the king, with Argob and with Arieh; and with him [were] fifty men of the sons of [the] Gileadites; and he killed him and reigned in his place.

R.25: Pekah son of Remaliah, one of Pekahiah's officers, made plans against him. He attacked Pekahiah, along with Argob and Arieh, in the strongest part of the royal palace in Samaria. Pekah had fifty men from Gilead with him. He killed Pekahiah and became king in his place.

decisions.choice: his officer: a high officer serving the king
decisions.reason: The word is related to "three" and may first have meant the third man in a chariot. In Kings it names an officer close to the king (7:2; 9:25). Pekah turned against the king he served.

decisions.choice: with Argob and with Arieh: probably two men killed with the king
alternatives: a place name displaced in copying
decisions.reason: The most natural reading is that Argob and Arieh were struck down together with Pekahiah, perhaps as his guards or officials. The words could also make them Pekah's helpers. Argob is also the name of a region east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 3:4), and Arieh means "the lion", so some think the words were once part of a place name and were displaced in copying. Their role cannot be settled.

decisions.choice: fifty men of the Gileadites: men from Gilead, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead was Israelite land east of the Jordan. Pekah's support came from there, and Gilead is among the lands lost to Assyria in his reign (verse 29).

decisions.choice: the citadel of the king's house: the fortified part of the palace
decisions.reason: The word means a strong tower or keep. The king was killed in the most secure part of his own palace.

decisions.choice: Pekah ... Pekahiah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the men where the Hebrew says "he" and "him", and put the fifty Gileadites in a sentence of their own. Readable says "one of Pekahiah's officers" and "the strongest part of the royal palace".

L.26: And the rest of the matters of Pekahiah and all that he did, look, they [are] written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

R.26: Everything else Pekahiah did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record of Israel, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Israel, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Pekahiah. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says "look, they are written" instead of asking "Are they not written?" (verse 6). Balanced and Readable state both forms the same way, with the source named as everywhere in Kings.

pieces: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.

L.27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty years.

R.27: Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in the fifty-second year that Azariah was king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for twenty years.

decisions.choice: the fifty-second year: Azariah's last year
decisions.reason: Azariah reigned fifty-two years (verse 2), so Pekah came to the throne in the year Azariah died.

decisions.choice: twenty years: a figure that seems to count more than his rule in Samaria
decisions.reason: The events dated by Assyrian records leave far fewer than twenty years between Menahem's payment to Pul and Hoshea's reign. One explanation is that the twenty years count from a time when Pekah already ruled part of the land, perhaps in Gilead, while Menahem and Pekahiah reigned in Samaria. The Hebrew does not explain the number.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable splits the accession formula, as in verse 8.

records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh; not he turned aside from [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he caused to sin Israel.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin.

L.28: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

R.28: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: the calf worship at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-33).

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded as in verse 9.

records.source: בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בָּא֮ תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֒ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־עִיּ֡וֹן וְאֶת־אָבֵ֣ל בֵּֽית־מַעֲכָ֡ה וְאֶת־יָ֠נוֹחַ וְאֶת־קֶ֨דֶשׁ וְאֶת־חָצ֤וֹר וְאֶת־הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְאֶת־הַגָּלִ֔ילָה כֹּ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ נַפְתָּלִ֑י וַיַּגְלֵ֖ם אַשּֽׁוּרָה׃
records.gloss: In [the] days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he took Ijon and Abel-beth-maacah and Janoah and Kedesh and Hazor and the Gilead and the Galilee, all [the] land of Naphtali; and he exiled them to Assyria.
pieces: During the reign of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came. He captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh and Hazor, as well as Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali. He took the people away into exile in Assyria.

L.29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came, and he took Ijon and Abel-beth-maacah and Janoah and Kedesh and Hazor and Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he exiled them to Assyria.

R.29: While Pekah was king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria attacked. He captured the towns of Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh and Hazor. He also took the regions of Gilead and Galilee, all the land of the tribe of Naphtali. He carried the people away to Assyria as captives.

decisions.choice: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria: the same king as Pul
decisions.reason: This is Tiglath-pileser the third, called Pul in verse 19. His campaign against Israel and Damascus is also known from Assyrian records, about 733-732 BC. Chapter 16 tells how Ahaz of Judah called him in (16:7-9).

decisions.choice: Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor: towns of the far north
decisions.reason: These towns lay on the route south from Damascus into Israel, north and west of the Sea of Galilee. Ijon and Abel-beth-maacah had been taken once before by Ben-hadad of Aram (1 Kings 15:20).

decisions.choice: Galilee, all the land of Naphtali: the second phrase explains the first
alternatives: Gilead and Galilee and all the land of Naphtali
decisions.reason: "All the land of Naphtali" most likely describes Galilee, the tribal land of Naphtali in the north. It could also be a third region in the list.

decisions.choice: he exiled them to Assyria: the first exile from Israel
decisions.reason: This is the first time Kings tells of Israelites carried off to Assyria. It looks ahead to the fall of Samaria and the exile of the whole northern kingdom (17:6, 23).

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people" for "them", which refers to the inhabitants of the lands named. Readable adds "the towns of", "the regions of" and "the tribe of" to help readers who do not know the places.

records.gloss: And conspired a conspiracy Hoshea son of Elah against Pekah son of Remaliah, and struck him and killed him, and reigned in his place, in year twenty of Jotham son of Uzziah.
pieces: Then Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah. He struck him down, killed him and became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

L.30: And Hoshea son of Elah conspired a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, and struck him and killed him, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

R.30: Then Hoshea son of Elah made plans against Pekah son of Remaliah. He attacked Pekah and killed him, and he became king in his place. This was in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

decisions.choice: Hoshea son of Elah: the last king of Israel
decisions.reason: Hoshea's reign and the fall of Samaria are told in 17:1-6. He is the fourth king in this chapter to take the throne by killing the king before him.

decisions.choice: the twentieth year of Jotham: a date counted beyond his sixteen years
decisions.reason: Jotham reigned sixteen years (verse 33), and 17:1 dates Hoshea's reign by Ahaz instead. The count here may run from when Jotham began to rule for his father (verse 5), or it may go on counting Jotham's years after Ahaz took over. The Hebrew does not explain it.

decisions.choice: conspired a conspiracy: formed a plot
decisions.reason: Verb and noun from the same root stress the act, as in verse 15.

decisions.choice: formed a conspiracy (Balanced); made plans against (Readable)
decisions.reason: English does not repeat the root; Balanced keeps the noun, and Readable uses the plain wording of verse 10. Readable names Pekah where the Hebrew says "him".

L.31: And the rest of the matters of Pekah and all that he did, look, they [are] written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

R.31: Everything else Pekah did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record of Israel, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Israel, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Pekah. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

R.32: Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah. It was the second year that Pekah son of Remaliah had been king of Israel.

decisions.choice: Jotham son of Uzziah: the son who had ruled for Azariah
decisions.reason: The account returns to Judah. Uzziah is the Azariah of verses 1-7, and Jotham had already governed for him during his disease (verse 5); now he reigns as king in his own right.

decisions.choice: reigned: became king
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, with a date the verb marks the start of the reign.

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date second
decisions.reason: Readable splits the accession formula, as in verse 1.

records.gloss: A son of twenty and five year[s] he was when he became king, and six-teen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
pieces: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.

L.33: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Jerusha daughter of Zadok.

R.33: He was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-five years: twenty-five years old
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Jerusha daughter of Zadok: the queen mother
decisions.reason: As for every king of Judah, Kings names his mother (verse 2). This Zadok is not otherwise known; the text does not say whether he belonged to the priestly family of that name.

records.gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh; according to all that had done Uzziah his father he did.
pieces: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his father Uzziah had done.

L.34: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; according to all that Uzziah his father had done, he did.

R.34: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, just as his father Uzziah had done.

decisions.choice: did the right in the eyes of Yahweh: the same verdict as his father's
decisions.reason: Jotham receives the verdict given to Uzziah (verse 3), with the same limit: the high places stayed (verse 35). 2 Chronicles 27:2 adds that, unlike his father, he did not enter the temple.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, as in verse 3. Balanced and Readable do not repeat the final "he did".

records.source: רַ֤ק הַבָּמוֹת֙ לֹ֣א סָ֔רוּ ע֗וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת ה֗וּא בָּנָ֛ה אֶת־שַׁ֥עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה הָעֶלְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Only the high places not were removed; still the people [were] sacrificing and making smoke at the high places; he built [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh, the upper.
pieces: However, the high places were not removed; the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.35: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense at the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.35: But the hilltop shrines were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the hilltop shrines. Jotham built the Upper Gate of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the high places
decisions.reason: As in verse 4: local shrines, kept in use against the law of the one place of worship (Deuteronomy 12:13-14).

decisions.choice: the upper gate of the house of Yahweh: a gate of the temple courts
decisions.reason: This gate seems to be the one on the north side of the temple, called the upper gate facing north in Ezekiel 9:2 and the upper Benjamin Gate in Jeremiah 20:2. "Built" may mean built anew or rebuilt. 2 Chronicles 27:3 tells of the same work.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines; temple; Jotham
decisions.reason: Readable says "hilltop shrines" as in verse 4, "temple" for "house" as it does throughout Kings, and names Jotham where the Hebrew says "he".

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jotham which he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Jotham, what he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.

L.36: And the rest of the matters of Jotham that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

R.36: Everything else Jotham did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: the royal record of Judah, now lost
decisions.reason: A court chronicle of the kingdom of Judah, which the writer of Kings used and points readers to for more about Jotham. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: The question form means "they are written there".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As with every use of this formula in Kings, the question stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable: "the Book of the History of the Kings of ..." (Balanced), "the history of the kings of ..." (Readable).

decisions.choice: the rest of the matters of Jotham: more is told in 2 Chronicles 27
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells of his building and of his war with the Ammonites (2 Chronicles 27:3-6).

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה לְהַשְׁלִ֨יחַ֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה רְצִ֖ין מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וְאֵ֖ת פֶּ֥קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: In the days the those began Yahweh to send against Judah Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.
pieces: In those days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began sending Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

L.37: In those days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began to send against Judah Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.

R.37: During that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began sending two kings to attack Judah: Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.

decisions.choice: Yahweh began to send: the attacks came from Yahweh
decisions.reason: The writer says that Yahweh himself sent these kings against Judah, as he later sends raiders against Judah in judgment (24:2). The attacks began under Jotham and came to a head under Ahaz.

decisions.choice: Rezin and Pekah: the joint attack on Judah
decisions.reason: The war of Aram and Israel against Judah is told in 16:5-9, and Isaiah's word to Ahaz about these two kings is in Isaiah 7:1-9.

decisions.choice: Aram: the kingdom whose capital was Damascus
decisions.reason: Aram lay north and east of Israel. Rezin was its last king before Assyria took Damascus (16:9).

decisions.choice: to attack Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "to attack" for "send against", which is what the phrase means here.

records.gloss: And lay down Jotham with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in [the] city of David his father, and reigned Ahaz his son in his place.
pieces: Then Jotham rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of his ancestor David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.

L.38: And Jotham lay down with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

R.38: Then Jotham died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: David his father: his ancestor David
decisions.reason: "Father" here means forefather; David was the founder of Jotham's royal line.

decisions.choice: Ahaz his son: the next king of Judah
decisions.reason: His reign is told in chapter 16.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula has one wording at each level. Balanced says "his ancestor David" for "David his father" (m2).
